questions.prompt: Who is allowed to edit shared or central files (routing, config, shared models)?
options: The first executor to claim them
questions.explanation: Shared/central files are orchestrator-owned. No executor may edit them; contracts depend on the orchestrator's result instead.

questions.prompt: Two contracts that must change the same file can still safely run in parallel.
questions.explanation: If two contracts must touch the same file they are not parallelizable — combine them into one contract or serialize them. Parallel safety requires disjoint scopes.

questions.prompt: The entire safety model reduces to which single idea?
options: Disjoint scopes plus isolated units of work merge cleanly and never leave the project broken
The orchestrator reviews every line of code
questions.explanation: Disjoint scopes + isolated units of work = parallel work that always merges cleanly and never leaves the project broken.

questions.prompt: During the JOIN step, what happens to an ABORTED contract?
options: Its partial work is merged anyway
It is retried automatically by the orchestrator
Its isolated workspace is confirmed discarded; the project is untouched
It blocks all other contracts from integrating
questions.explanation: On join, ABORTED means the workspace is discarded and the project is left exactly as it was. Only ACCEPTED contracts are integrated, in dependency order.

questions.prompt: Done is asserted by the executor, not proven.
questions.explanation: Done is proven, not asserted. The contract names the verification, and it must pass before the work is accepted.
